content.intro: Print a Ship Captain Crew score sheet that adds up every player's cargo, or keep score on your phone. Pick 5, 10 or 20 rounds online.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. On your turn, roll all five dice up to three times. You need a 6 (the ship), then a 5 (the captain), then a 4 (the crew), in that order; set each aside as you get it.

Once you have all three, the other two dice are your cargo and their total is your score, from 2 to 12. If you have rolls left you may reroll both cargo dice to try for more. Without a ship, captain and crew after three rolls, you score 0.

Write each player's cargo in the round's row. After the last round the highest total wins. Bar games often play single rounds for the best cargo instead; the sheet works for that too, just compare the row.

faqs.q: How do you score Ship Captain Crew?
faqs.a: Once you have a 6, a 5 and a 4 (ship, captain and crew), the other two dice are your cargo, and their total is your score for the turn. If you don't get all three in three rolls, you score 0.

faqs.q: Do you have to get the ship, captain and crew in order?
faqs.a: Yes. A 5 counts only once you have a 6, and a 4 only once you have the 5. If you roll a 5 and a 4 with no 6, you roll all the dice again.
Yes, if you still have rolls left. Most players reroll both cargo dice together, and the last roll stands.

faqs.q: What is the best score in Ship Captain Crew?
How many rounds do you play?
faqs.a: As many as you like. Bar games often play one round at a time for the best cargo; for a longer game, add up the cargo over 5, 10 or 20 rounds.

faqs.q: How many dice do you need?
faqs.a: Five ordinary dice and a cup, shared by everyone. Any number of people can play.
